title: Financial Aid Map
creator: Beth Kullberg
subject: College Admissions
description: An explorable map of where financial aid comes from (federal, state, institutional, private), the forms it takes, and which kinds are need-based or merit-based.

learningObjectives: Students will classify types of financial aid by source (federal, state, institutional, private), form (grant, scholarship, loan, work-study), and basis (need or merit), and explain which kinds must be repaid.

controls: Show only gift aid, Show only need-based, Show only what the FAFSA unlocks, and Show all buttons

keyQuestions: Why is a dollar of grant aid worth more than a dollar of loan aid?
Which aid can you get only by filling out a separate application?
Why should a family file the FAFSA even if they don't expect need-based aid?
commonMisconceptions: All financial aid is free money.
Only low-income families should file the FAFSA.
assessmentOpportunities: Students classify six aid examples by source, form, and basis, and correctly say which must be repaid.
